_description: Pre-audit snapshot of NeuraForge state. Reconstructed from git history (commit 96929e5 and earlier), results files in results/activation_ablation/ and results/optimizer_comparison/, and verification_report.md Phase 4 output. This captures the state before any fixes were applied.
_reconstruction_note: The original pre-fix state was never formally captured as a JSON snapshot at the time. This file was reconstructed after the fact from surviving artifacts. Entries marked 'source' indicate where each data point came from.

findings.basic_ops: all PASS (add, sub, mul, div, matmul, sum, mean, exp, log, pow)
findings.reshape: FAIL — 1.00e+08 relative error (later found to be a harness bug, not an engine bug)
findings.transpose: FAIL — 1.00e+08 relative error (later found to be a harness bug, not an engine bug)
findings.broadcasting: all 22 shape pairs PASS for add/sub/mul/div

transformer.detail: Script train_shakespeare.py existed but was never run. results/shakespeare/ directory did not exist. No training artifacts, no loss curves, no generated text.

cnn_accuracy.detail: This accuracy was from an MLP, not a CNN. The CNN had never been trained.

ablations_pre_fix.protocol: single seed (std = 0.0), fixed LR (not swept), no validation split for tuning
ablations_pre_fix.why_invalid: All activations used the same fixed LR=0.05. Optimizer comparison used fixed LRs (SGD=0.1, Adam=0.001, NeuroGrad=0.1) without sweeping. Single seed means zero statistical power. The comparison was structurally unfair in both directions.

scaling_claim_pre_fix.original_claim: NeuraForge achieves 3.96 ms/step compared to PyTorch's 3.58 ms/step — almost as fast
scaling_claim_pre_fix.why_invalid: Measured on a tiny MLP where both frameworks dispatch to the same BLAS backend. The comparison measured BLAS against BLAS, not framework against framework.

test_suite.failed_test: test_readme_matches_results — README was out of sync with performance numbers
